Name: Rust Software Factory
Documentation: Architecture of the software factory itself: how a business need becomes rolled-out Rust software, with AI agents doing the work and a human holding the gates.

Name: Product owner
Documentation: The human who owns the business outcome and approves the factory's gates.

Name: Business needs change often
Documentation: Business rules and priorities change; software must follow quickly without decaying.

Name: Healthy, maintainable software
Documentation: Code stays easy to change over years: clear boundaries, strong tests, recorded decisions.

Name: Every change is traceable
Documentation: Any line of code can be traced back to the business need that caused it, and forward to its release.

Name: Development cost under control
Documentation: Expensive AI models are used only where their reasoning is needed.

Name: Every change through a reviewed PR
Documentation: main is protected; nothing reaches it without a pull request and a human merge.

Name: Architecture documented in TOGAF / ArchiMate
Documentation: Business, information and technology architecture is kept as an ArchiMate model and TOGAF documents, so business-side changes can be analysed.

Name: Route tasks to models by difficulty
Documentation: Simple, clear tasks go to Sonnet, hard ones to Opus, search to Haiku; the conductor runs on Fable.

Name: Human approver
Documentation: Signs off architecture, merges PRs, promotes pilot to production.

Name: Conductor
Documentation: Plans, designs the architecture, splits work into tasks and routes each to a worker.

Name: Worker
Documentation: Carries out one task in its own git worktree and delivers it as a PR.

Name: Software delivery lifecycle
Documentation: From business need to production rollout.

Name: Plan and design
Documentation: Vision, epics, stories, architecture model and ADRs (TOGAF A–D).

Name: Implement task
Documentation: Code and tests for one task on its own branch.

Name: Review and merge
Documentation: Automated gates plus human merge of the PR.

Name: Accept build
Documentation: Acceptance tests run against the release image.

Name: Pilot and roll out
Documentation: Deploy to the pilot host, then to production after approval.

Name: User story
Documentation: A small piece of user-visible behaviour with Gherkin acceptance criteria.

Name: Architecture decision record
Documentation: Why a significant decision was made, and what else was considered.

Name: Conductor agent (Fable)
Documentation: Main Claude Code session, model claude-fable-5-2.

Name: Hard worker (Opus)
Documentation: Subagent on claude-opus-5-5 for ambiguous or cross-crate tasks.

Name: Simple worker (Sonnet)
Documentation: Subagent on claude-sonnet-5-5 for clear, single-crate tasks.

Name: Scout (Haiku)
Documentation: Subagent on claude-haiku-5-5 for search and context gathering.

Name: GitHub
Documentation: Issues, Project board, pull requests and Actions CI.

Name: Issue
Documentation: Epic, story, requirement, task, bug, change request or ADR request.

Name: Pull request
Documentation: A proposed change with traceability links and test evidence.

Name: Developer workstation
Documentation: Arch Linux desktop or Ubuntu on WSL, set up by bootstrap.sh.

Name: Rust toolchain
Documentation: Pinned in rust-toolchain.toml, with cargo tools pinned in mise.toml.

Name: Archi
Documentation: Builds the ArchiMate model and HTML report from the text model.

Name: Podman
Documentation: Runs the application containers on every host.

Name: Container registry (GHCR)
Documentation: Stores the release images, built once and promoted unchanged.

Name: Pilot host
Documentation: First deploy target for a release.

Name: Production hosts
Documentation: Receive the release after the pilot is approved.
